### Core Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework Papers

- **AutoGen:** [AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155)  
  *Authors:* Qingyun Wu et al.  
  Introduces conversable, customizable agents integrating LLMs, human input, and tools to execute complex task workflows.
- **MetaGPT:** [MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352)  
  *Authors:* Sirui Hong et al.  
  Encodes Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into structured agent communication flows for multi-agent software engineering.
- **ChatDev:** [Communicative Agents for Software Development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07924)  
  *Authors:* Chen Qian et al.  
  Introduces a chat-chain structure decomposing the software development lifecycle into sequential multi-agent dialogues.

### Comprehensive Survey and Review Papers

- **Foundational Survey:** [Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01680)  
  *Authors:* Taicheng Guo et al.  
  Covers agent profiling, multi-agent communication schemes, environment simulation, and benchmarks.
- **Communication Architectures:** [Beyond Self-Talk: A Communication-Centric Survey of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14321)  
  *Authors:* Bingyu Yan et al.  
  Examines system topologies, interaction protocols, and scalability bottlenecks.
- **Workflow Orchestration:** [A Survey on Agent Workflow -- Status and Future](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01186)  
  *Authors:* Chaojia Yu et al.  
  Classifies pipeline vs. graph orchestration flows, role assignment, and workflow specifications across 20+ systems.
- **Collaboration & Evolution:** [Beyond Individual Intelligence: Surveying Collaboration, Failure Attribution, and Self-Evolution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14892)  
  *Authors:* Shihao Qi et al.  
  Presents the LIFE framework addressing multi-round error propagation and collective self-refinement.
- **Debate Topologies:** [Multi-Agent Debate Strategies: Survey, Taxonomy, and Challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26212)  
  *Authors:* Quim Motger et al.  
  Synthesizes 141 studies focusing on interaction structures, memory, and consensus protocols in multi-agent debate.
- **Communication Theory:** [The Five Ws of Multi-Agent Communication: Who Talks to Whom, When, What, and Why -- A Survey from MARL to Emergent Language and LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11583)  
  *Authors:* Jingdi Chen et al.  
  Maps agent coordination trade-offs across reinforcement learning and LLM paradigms.

### Agent Comparison and Missing Information
- **Findings Agreement:** Agents targeted complementary areas. One agent retrieved primary framework papers; the other retrieved taxonomy and survey papers. No factual contradictions occurred between sources.
- **Missing Scope:** Neither agent covered non-LLM classic multi-agent systems or industrial production runtimes beyond research publications.

### Task: Search for comprehensive survey and review research papers on LLM multi-agent orchestration architectures and collaboration patterns.
- Status: COMPLETED (Worker: worker_survey_papers_e54652f8, Tab: tab_survey_papers_8103dd)
- Findings: #### Comprehensive Survey and Review Papers on LLM Multi-Agent Orchestration & Collaboration

- **[Beyond Individual Intelligence: Surveying Collaboration, Failure Attribution, and Self-Evolution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14892)**
  - **Authors:** Shihao Qi, Jie Ma, Rui Xing, Wei Guo, Xiao Huang, Zhitao Gao, Jianhao Deng, et al.
  - **arXiv ID:** `arXiv:2605.14892`
  - **Focus & Patterns:** Establishes the **LIFE** progression model (*Lay foundations, Integrate through collaboration, Find faults through attribution, Evolve through self-improvement*). Analyzes error propagation across orchestration rounds and multi-agent collective self-refinement.

- **[Beyond Self-Talk: A Communication-Centric Survey of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14321)**
  - **Authors:** Bingyu Yan, Zhibo Zhou, Litian Zhang, Lian Zhang, Ziyi Zhou, Dezhuang Miao, Zhoujun Li, Chaozhuo Li, Xiaoming Zhang
  - **arXiv ID:** `arXiv:2502.14321` (Accepted by *Frontiers of Computer Science*, DOI: 10.1007/s11704-026-50857-y)
  - **Focus & Patterns:** Reviews multi-agent systems via a dual-layer communication taxonomy: system-level orchestration (topologies, coordination goals, protocols) and internal communication (interaction strategies, message paradigms, content negotiation, efficiency, and scalability bottlenecks).

- **[A Survey on Agent Workflow -- Status and Future](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01186)**
  - **Authors:** Chaojia Yu, Zihan Cheng, Hanwen Cui, Yishuo Gao, Zexu Luo, Yijin Wang, Hangbin Zheng, Yong Zhao
  - **arXiv ID:** `arXiv:2508.01186` (Published in *IEEE ICAIBD 2025*)
  - **Focus & Patterns:** Analyzes structured workflow orchestration frameworks across 20+ systems. Classifies agent interaction architectures into role assignment, pipeline vs. graph orchestration flows, workflow specification formats, and execution security.

- **[Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01680)**
  - **Authors:** Taicheng Guo, Xiuying Chen, Yaqi Wang, Ruidi Chang, Shichao Pei, Nitesh V. Chawla, Olaf Wiest, Xiangliang Zhang
  - **arXiv ID:** `arXiv:2402.01680`
  - **Focus & Patterns:** Foundational survey covering agent profiling, multi-agent communication schemes, environment simulation, collective growth/learning mechanisms, and standard multi-agent evaluation benchmarks.

- **[Multi-Agent Debate Strategies: Survey, Taxonomy, and Challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26212)**
  - **Authors:** Quim Motger, Marc Oriol, Jordi Marco, Xavier Franch
  - **arXiv ID:** `arXiv:2607.26212` (Under review at *ACM Computing Surveys*)
  - **Focus & Patterns:** Systematic literature review synthesizing 141 primary studies on Multi-Agent Debate (MAD). Formalizes participant roles, exchange interaction structures (topologies, memory), and consensus/agreement protocols.

- **[The Five Ws of Multi-Agent Communication: Who Talks to Whom, When, What, and Why -- A Survey from MARL to Emergent Language and LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11583)**
  - **Authors:** Jingdi Chen, Hanqing Yang, Zongjun Liu, Carlee Joe-Wong
  - **arXiv ID:** `arXiv:2602.11583` (Accepted at *Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR)*)
  - **Focus & Patterns:** Traces multi-agent collaboration across MARL, emergent language, and LLM orchestration using the Five Ws framework, detailing natural-language priors, dynamic topologies, and coordination trade-offs.
